evals.prompt: I'm about to run git commit on a batch of staged files for the auth service — make sure no API keys or tokens slipped into the diff before I push.
evals.expected_output: A scan of only staged files via `vulnetix secrets --staged-only -o json`, a redacted findings table grouped by type with confidence levels, and a written summary at .vulnetix/secrets/<timestamp>.summary.yaml.
expectations: Reads .vulnetix/capabilities.yaml and confirms binaries.git is present before invoking --staged-only
Runs `vulnetix secrets --staged-only -o json` (or `vulnetix scan --evaluate-secrets`) producing JSON written to .vulnetix/secrets.<timestamp>.json
Resolves the staged file list with `git diff --cached --name-only` rather than scanning the full repo
Renders a table with columns Type, File:Line, Snippet (redacted), Confidence and redacts ~60% of every detected secret value
Writes a sanitized summary record to .vulnetix/secrets/<timestamp>.summary.yaml containing counts by type and file paths but no raw secret values

evals.prompt: We just got a customer report that an AWS access key showed up in our public repo — do a full repo audit and produce a rotation list for whatever leaked.
evals.expected_output: Full-repo `vulnetix secrets` run, a high-confidence findings table (AWS/GitHub PAT/Slack/Stripe), per-provider rotation/revocation guidance, and history-rewrite warnings for committed leaks.
expectations: Runs `vulnetix secrets -o json` against the whole repo (no --staged-only, no --paths narrowing) and captures JSON output
Separates high-confidence matches (AWS / GitHub PAT / Slack / Stripe regex hits) from medium-confidence generic high-entropy strings in the rendered table
Emits per-provider rotation/revocation steps (e.g. AWS IAM key rotation, GitHub PAT revoke, Slack token rotate, Stripe key roll) keyed on each unique secret type found
For secrets in committed files (not just working tree) recommends `git filter-repo` or BFG repo-cleaner and strongly advises rotation since the value is in git history
Never prints the un-redacted secret value anywhere in the response (every snippet shows ~60% replaced with `*`)

evals.prompt: Scan only the three files I just touched — src/config.ts, src/db.ts, deploy/env.sh — and tell me if anything in there will trip our CI secret gate.
evals.expected_output: Path-scoped scan via `vulnetix secrets --paths`, redacted findings on those three files, a CI-gate verdict driven by high-confidence matches, and a sanitized memory summary.
expectations: Calls `vulnetix secrets --paths src/config.ts src/db.ts deploy/env.sh -o json` (or equivalent `vulnetix scan --evaluate-secrets --paths ...`) and does not scan files outside that list
Renders the standard Type / File:Line / Snippet (redacted) / Confidence table scoped to those three paths
Calls out whether any finding is high-confidence (AWS/GitHub PAT/Slack/Stripe) versus medium-confidence high-entropy so the CI gate decision is explicit
Mentions inline suppression via `# pix-ignore-secret` on the next line for any legitimate false positive rather than removing the detector
Appends a sanitized record to .vulnetix/secrets/<timestamp>.summary.yaml (counts by type and file paths, no values) as a single consolidated memory write
